product.name: Shelfie
product.tagline: Your price list, open to AI shoppers.
product.audience: Small sellers with a paper price list and no website, such as home bakers
valueProps: A photo of a paper price list becomes a PayPal catalog and a live shop
Any AI assistant finds the shop's agent door from its web address and orders through it
Buyers pay with PayPal, straight into the seller's own PayPal account

timeline.screen: Clip 01: the handwritten Marigold menu on a counter, zooming in slowly.
timeline.narration: AI assistants have started shopping for people. But PayPal's agent checkout is built for merchants with a website store. Rosa bakes from her kitchen. She has no website. She has this sheet of paper. In a US Census survey, 47 percent of food and lodging businesses had no website. An assistant can't order from a sheet of paper.

onScreen.text: PayPal's agent checkout “is limited to Store Sync customers today”, for merchants “using their existing website storefronts”.
47% of US accommodation and food-service employer firms reported having no website.
onScreen.source: US Census Bureau, Annual Survey of Entrepreneurs (data year 2016)

timeline.screen: Clip 02: phone, Snap your price list, the Marigold photo, Reading your menu, then Check your menu (cut on the result).
timeline.narration: Shelfie starts with one photo. Rosa snaps her price list, and Claude reads it.

timeline.screen: Clip 03: the review questions (“2 for $7”, set $3.50 each), Looks right, Your PayPal email (drawn as dots), Publish, Adding to PayPal, Your shop is live.
timeline.narration: Shelfie only asks about what it isn't sure of, like a price written as two for seven dollars. Rosa adds her PayPal email, so buyers pay her directly. Every item becomes a product in PayPal's catalog. In our tests, photo to live shop took 8 to 14 seconds of machine time.

timeline.screen: Clip 03b: laptop, Menu tab, Snap your counter, the display-case photo, Finding your items, the two croissant crops, Use on each, the thumbnails fill in.
timeline.narration: One more photo, of her display case. Claude finds each item in it, and crops its photo.

timeline.screen: Clip 04: Share tab, Print counter card, the card with the QR code and the agent door.
timeline.narration: The shop gets an agent door, and a card for the counter. Regulars scan it, or give the shop's link to their own assistant.

timeline.screen: Clip 05 (sped up about 2x): Claude Code in an empty folder, given only the shop URL; it fetches the page, finds the agent door, calls get_shop_info, list_products, create_order, and prints a PayPal approval link.
timeline.narration: This is Claude Code, given nothing but the shop's web address. The page tells it where the agent door is. It reads the menu, places the order, and hands back a PayPal approval link.

timeline.screen: Clip 06: the shop page, Order with an assistant, the nut-allergy request, the Activity panel, the warning that almond croissants contain nuts, the confirmation, create_order, Approve on PayPal.
timeline.narration: Buyers without an assistant get one right on the shop page. This buyer wants almond croissants, and mentions a nut allergy. The assistant warns that they contain nuts. The buyer confirms, and it places the order.

timeline.screen: Clip 06b (after the login, which is cut): PayPal's review page with the total, Complete Purchase, the receipt: Paid, paid to Marigold Bakehouse's own PayPal account (masked).
timeline.narration: The buyer logs in to PayPal and approves. Shelfie captures the payment, and the money lands in Rosa's own PayPal account, not ours.

timeline.screen: Clip 07: terminal, create_order with a price of 0.01 is refused: INVALID_ARGUMENTS, prices are set by the shop.
timeline.narration: And agents can't set prices. The server checks that, not the model.

timeline.screen: Clip 08: the dashboard's Orders tab, To prepare, the new order paid with its AI brief and the nut-allergy warning; the order page with Paid to (masked), the PayPal order and transaction ids, the timeline.
timeline.narration: Rosa's dashboard shows the order as paid. A Claude agent reads PayPal's record of the order through the PayPal Agent Toolkit, and writes her a brief. It catches the nut allergy, so she can check with the buyer before shipping.

timeline.screen: Clip 09: Add tracking, USPS and a number, Saved; then in the console, Where's my order?, get_order_status, the tracking number.
timeline.narration: She adds tracking, and the buyer's assistant reads it back.

timeline.screen: Clip 10: the architecture card: photo, Claude vision, PayPal catalog, agent door found from the shop page, PayPal Orders v2 paid to the seller, capture, Agent Toolkit brief.
timeline.narration: Shelfie turns a paper price list into a shop that any AI assistant can find, order from, and pay with PayPal. The money goes straight to the seller. Agent shopping shouldn't be only for shops with a website. For Rosa, a sheet of paper is enough.

timeline.note: End card: the Shelfie mark, name and line. No narration.
timeline.title: Shelfie
timeline.subtitle: Your price list, open to AI shoppers.
timeline.cta: Built with PayPal Orders v2, the PayPal Agent Toolkit and Claude
